feature: Go exports read whole by every reader
description: Every name of a Go const or var spec is an export and a graph entity, grouped or not, and the API contract reader keeps struct fields by Go's Unicode export rule.

specs.description: A multi-name const spec exports every name it declares, at the spec's line, as a value
specs.given: A Go file whose line 3 is `const A, B = 1, 2`
specs.when: The analyzer extracts the file's exports through AstPort::extract_exports with Language::Go
specs.then: There are two exports: `A` and `B`. Each is at line 3 and has kind Value

specs.description: A grouped const spec with several names exports every name
specs.given: A Go file with `const (` on line 1, `X, Y = 1, 2` on line 2, `Z = 3` on line 3, and `)` on line 4
specs.when: The analyzer extracts the file's exports
specs.then: The exports are `X` at line 2, `Y` at line 2 and `Z` at line 3. All three have kind Value

specs.description: The commas between names are not names
specs.given: A Go file with `const A, B, C = 1, 2, 3`
specs.when: The analyzer extracts the file's exports
specs.then: The export names are exactly `A`, `B` and `C`. No export has the name `,`, an empty name, or any name that is not one of the declared identifiers

specs.description: An unexported second name of a const spec is not an export
specs.given: A Go file with `const A, b = 1, 2`
specs.when: The analyzer extracts the file's exports
specs.then: `A` is an export and `b` is not

specs.description: An unused second const name is a dead export, like the same name written alone
specs.given: A Go project where one file declares `const A, B = 1, 2`, and another file in the package names `A` but no file other than the declaring one names `B`
specs.then: `B` is reported as a dead export at the spec's line, and `A` is not

specs.description: Every exported name of every const spec is an export at the spec's line
specs.given: Any Go file of const specs, grouped or ungrouped, each declaring one or more identifiers on its line
specs.when: The analyzer extracts the file's exports
specs.then: The const exports are exactly the declared identifiers that Go exports, one per identifier. Each has kind Value and the line of its own spec. A const spec and a var spec with the same names produce the same set of names

specs.description: A struct field whose first letter is a non-ASCII upper-case letter is in the API contract
specs.given: A Go file declaring `type Report struct { Ärger string; Count int }` that the API contract reads
specs.when: The contract reader extracts the file's API facts through AstPort::extract_api
specs.then: The TypeDecl for `Report` has a Struct body with a field for `Ärger` and a field for `Count`

specs.description: A field whose first character is not upper-case is not in the contract, ASCII or not
specs.given: A Go struct with the fields `ärger string`, `count int`, `_hidden int` and `Name string`
specs.when: The contract reader extracts the file's API facts
specs.then: The struct body has only the `Name` field. `ärger`, `count` and `_hidden` are absent

specs.description: The contract reader and the analyzer agree on which names are exported
specs.when: The contract reader decides whether to keep the field
specs.then: It keeps the field exactly when the field's first character is a Unicode upper-case letter. This is the same verdict the analyzer gives for a top-level name spelled the same way

specs.given: A Go file with `var (` on line 1, `Alpha = 1` on line 2, `Beta = 2` on line 3, and `)` on line 4
specs.when: The code graph extracts the file's entities
specs.then: `Alpha` is an entity of kind Const at line 2, and `Beta` is an entity of kind Const at line 3

specs.description: Every name of a multi-name spec is a code-graph entity
specs.given: A Go file whose line 5 is `const P, Q = 1, 2` and whose line 6 is `var M, N = 3, 4`
specs.when: The code graph extracts the file's entities
specs.then: `P` and `Q` are entities of kind Const at line 5, and `M` and `N` are entities of kind Const at line 6

specs.description: Graph consumers report the users of a grouped var
specs.given: A Go package where one file declares `Beta` inside a `var ( … )` group and another file uses `Beta`
specs.then: The using file is listed as a consumer, and `Beta` is not reported safe to remove

specs.description: The graph does not invent entities from separators or skip any declared name
specs.given: A Go file with `var (` and then `A, B = 1, 2` inside the group, closed by `)`
specs.when: The code graph extracts the file's entities
specs.then: The const/var entities are exactly `A` and `B`. There is no entity for `,`, for `var_spec_list`, or for an empty name, and neither `A` nor `B` is missing

specs.description: The code graph and the analyzer agree on what a Go const or var export is
specs.given: Any Go file of const and var declarations, grouped or not, with any number of names per spec
specs.when: The analyzer extracts exports and the code graph extracts entities
specs.then: For every exported name, the analyzer has an export of kind Value at a line L exactly when the graph has an entity of kind Const with the same name at line L
